name: problem
text: Soft skills matter in engineering education. This project investigates whether interview language and vocal delivery can support their estimation, using personality as an intermediate step.

name: research-question
text: Research question
textPreview: Research question

name: question
text: Can LLM-derived text cues and audio characteristics predict interview ratings and support an exploratory Big Five-to-BESSI skill mapping?
textPreview: Can LLM-derived text cues and audio characteristics predict interview ratings and support an exploratory Big Five-to-BESSI skill mapping?

name: objectives
text: Objectives
textPreview: Objectives

name: objective-list
text:
1. Extract structured language and audio features.
2. Compare predictions with simple baselines and published RecruitView results.
3. Evaluate a separate personality-to-skill mapping and identify its limits.

name: literature
text: RecruitView [1] provides interview personality and performance ratings. BESSI research [2, 3] studies related personality and skill measures. Relatedness supports testing a mapping, not assuming that personality and skills are equivalent.

name: limits
text:
Limits: no direct BESSI labels in RecruitView; emotion cues lack independent validation; engineering-student generalisation is untested.
Follow-up test analyses are exploratory. Research use only; do not use these estimates for hiring decisions.
